concepts.def: A rotating black hole solution to GR.
Region outside the event horizon where frame dragging forces co-rotation.
Dragging of spacetime around a rotating mass.
Extracting rotational energy by splitting an object inside the ergosphere.

walkthroughs.body_html: Roy Kerr found the rotating solution in 1963. A Kerr black hole has an event horizon and, outside it, an ergosphere where spacetime itself is dragged around the spin axis.
Inside the ergosphere, frame dragging forces every observer to co-rotate. You can still escape, but you cannot stand still relative to distant stars.

Roger Penrose proposed in 1969 a process where a particle splits inside the ergosphere; one piece falls in with negative energy and the other escapes with more energy than the original — extracting rotational energy.
